Tactical decisions made during the tournament, including the choice to field four frontline bowlers with Jasprit Bumrah as the lone fast bowler alongside multiple spinners on turning surfaces, were credited as a key factor in the team's success. Pakistan mounted a strong chase, coming close to the target, but fell short against India's spin-heavy bowling attack featuring lone specialist fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah. In analysis shared on India Today, it was noted that tactical flexibility, squad depth, and the demanding environment of the Indian Premier League contribute significantly to India's continued advantage over Pakistan in Twenty20 cricket. The victory marked consecutive cricket gold medals for India at the Asian Games, taking the contingent's gold medal count to 19 as India aims to surpass Uzbekistan for fourth place in the overall standings.

India Beat Pakistan To Win Asian Games Cricket Gold, Clinch 19th Gold MedalThe Indian men's cricket team secured the gold medal at the Asian Games by defeating arch-rivals Pakistan by 19 runs in the final, taking India's gold tally at the games to 19. Batting first, India posted a total of 211 runs in their 20 overs, driven by half-centuries from Abhishek Sharma, who scored 61, and Tilak Varma, who remained unbeaten on 51. In response, Pakistan managed 192 for six in their 20 overs, despite Hasan Nawaz's fighting knock of 96 runs. Standout bowling performances by spinners Axar Patel and Washington Sundar, who took two wickets each, alongside part-time bowler Shivam Dube's two wickets, helped restrict Pakistan. This victory marks India's second consecutive Asian Games gold medal in cricket following their triumph in Hangzhou in 2023. The victory also highlights India's ongoing dominance over Pakistan in the shortest format, having won 15 of their last 18 T20 encounters.
